title: Heat Pumps Need One Thing to BEAT Gas Boilers (Most Homes Don't Have It)
summary: A UK installer argues that with electricity about four times the price of gas, a heat pump only matches an efficient boiler on running cost, and that solar, batteries and off-peak tariffs are what make it pay.

assertions.quote: because it's moving heat rather than creating it, it is way more efficient
that current spark gap means it isn't automatically cheaper to run than say a high efficiency gas boiler

verdicts.note: A higher elec-to-gas price ratio (4.1 at 2019 prices vs 3.3) cuts gas homes with positive bill savings from 32-92% to 22-83%; it worsens the economics but most efficient units still beat gas.

Whether a high price ratio makes heat pumps costlier depends on seasonal COP: break-even is ratio times AFUE, ranging from 1.6 (Florida) to 6.1 (Alaska) at 2024 prices, with 30 states needing COP 3 or more.
In RMI's Providence model, a cold climate, a leaky home and relatively high electricity prices together make a heat pump retrofit cost more than gas.

Edwards notes that higher electricity prices reduce the benefit of replacing a furnace with a heat pump, and its robustness checks find electricity price negatively correlated with heat pump use where direct fuels dominate.

LBNL: some electrification projects raised energy costs by up to $1,000/yr, confirmed to come from higher electricity use paired with high regional rates (MA $0.184, CA $0.169, VT $0.154/kWh); savings were large mainly where oil or propane was displaced.

With New England's high electricity-to-gas price ratio, the gas break-even temperature was above 70 F, so a mini-split 'does not offer a viable direct replacement for a gas-fired system at today's energy prices'.

UK heat pump households (measured consumption times retail prices) pay about £190/yr more to run a heat pump than a gas boiler at Octopus standard rates (£323 at government 2024 prices), with electricity about 4x the price of gas per kWh; disconnecting from gas trims about £100/yr off the gap.
Modelled for Edmonton: much lower gas prices with similar electricity rates, plus cold weather, make gas with AC (or a hybrid) the cheapest option and all-electric heat pumps less competitive.

assertions.quote: There isn't a huge leap between these two technologies when it comes to the running costs.

verdicts.note: For gas-heated homes with AC, the share with lower bills ranges from 38% (minimum-efficiency, median -$70/yr) to 99% (cold-climate high-efficiency, median $380/yr), and only 5-58% for gas homes without AC; it holds only for efficient equipment.
At 2024 average prices a seasonal COP of 2.5 beats a 95% furnace in only 11 states; 30 states need COP 3 or more, so it depends on location and efficiency.
Edwards says heat pumps are cost-effective in many places but can cost more to operate than gas furnaces, especially in colder regions, so the blanket claim fails.
In RMI's gas retrofits, heat pump households pay more for energy in Chicago and Providence and save too little to recover the extra capital in Houston and Oakland.

At 2015-16 Massachusetts/Rhode Island prices, the break-even temperature against an 80%-efficient gas system was above 70 F (above 58 F for cold-climate units), so a mini-split was essentially never cheaper to run than gas; the test units were 2012-14 models (a modelled HSPF-13 unit moves the break-even to 28-40 F).
Survey comments from participants who had gas repeatedly said bills were higher than with natural gas; this is anecdotal (no billing analysis, small affiliated sample).

In the UK at 2024 prices on a standard flat tariff, heat pumps cost about £190 more per year to run than the gas boilers they replaced (boilers, not furnaces); only a heat pump time-of-use tariff reverses this.

Canadian lifetime-cost modelling finds heat pumps beat gas heating plus AC in nearly all cases in Montreal, Halifax and Vancouver and usually in Toronto with gas backup, but not in many Edmonton cases; the comparison also counts cooling and equipment.

assertions.quote: having an air source heat pump rather than one of those boilers is going to be way cheaper to run

verdicts.note: Homes heating with electricity, oil or propane that have AC see lower bills in 95-100% of cases (median $300-$650/yr); 73-86% without AC; still 87-99% (propane) and 66-100% (oil) at 2019 prices.
In Edwards' county model, where homes heat with electricity (resistance) or non-gas fuels, heating is generally more expensive and heat pump bill savings are higher.
In Providence, RMI's heat pumps have a lower 15-year net present cost than both oil and propane systems, and save at least $10,000 against propane.
Measured cost savings averaged 33% against propane furnaces and 53% against electric resistance in Minnesota homes; oil was not tested, so the claim is supported for two of its three fuels.

Mini-splits were cheaper to run than electric resistance and propane at all observed temperatures, but against oil they were cheaper only above a price-dependent break-even (about 32 F in 2016, 12 F in 2015).
In the UK, households previously on electric heating used less electricity after a heat pump, which supports the resistance-heat part; oil and propane are not tested.
Heat pumps use up to 65% less energy than electric baseboards, which supports the resistance-heat part; oil and propane are not modelled.

assertions.quote: an air source heat pump right now, on average, is about 4.3 times higher than a gas boiler install

verdicts.note: Replacing the existing heater with a minimum-efficiency heat pump costs an average of $6,600 more than replacing it like-for-like.
In cold-climate homes without central AC, the mean incremental cost over a furnace alone is $3,000, $15,000 and $18,000 for the three heat pump tiers.

From Edwards' national cost medians, a heat pump costs $6,185 while a gas furnace plus AC costs $6,455 and the AC alone $4,684, which puts the furnace alone at roughly $1,800, far below the heat pump.
RMI finds that customers with existing gas service face higher upfront costs to retrofit to electric space and water heating than to install new gas devices.

LBNL: among 2,298 HVAC measures, fuel-fired heating systems averaged $3,000 less than heat pump installations (heat pump median $8,027 vs furnace median $5,025 in 2019 dollars), though heat pumps also provide cooling.
Database costs put an air source heat pump at $2,994-$5,550 versus a propane furnace at $2,060-$3,900; a propane rather than gas furnace, and cost estimates rather than quotes.
UK figures: an air-source heat pump installation averaged £12,713 before the grant (£5,213 after it) against an assumed £2,250 gas boiler; this compares with a UK boiler rather than a furnace.

Canadian mid-case capital costs for a detached home: gas furnace about $3,750 to $6,030 against $7,570 to $13,260 for a standard ducted air-source heat pump and $14,840 to $19,880 for a cold-climate one (the heat pump also replaces the AC).

assertions.quote: you should be able to get a grant for 7 and 1/2 thousand pounds towards the cost of moving away from a gas boiler

verdicts.note: The UK Boiler Upgrade Scheme started in May 2022 at £5,000 per air-source heat pump and rose to £7,500 from 23 October 2023.

assertions.quote: usually a poorly designed system that's been installed on the cheap will cost more to run
if you remove your gas meter, then you won't have to pay standing charges

verdicts.note: Fully disconnecting gas removes the fixed customer or standing charge, typically worth around £100 a year in the UK and $100-300 in the US.

Homes that convert all gas end uses and shut off service no longer pay the fixed charge (median $11.25/month in 2015, up to $34-$65 in Chicago and NYC); dropping it raises gas homes with positive savings from 32-92% to 49-97%.
Average gas prices include fixed customer charges: a household keeping its gas connection keeps paying it, one that disconnects saves it.
RMI notes that many gas bills carry a fixed monthly service charge ($33/month in its Chicago scenario), which only full home electrification removes.
UK customers pay about £100/yr for a mains gas connection, and a heat pump that allows full disconnection removes that charge.
A Montreal household that disconnects from gas would save over $4,000 in fixed gas fees over the system's life ($228/yr over 18 years).

assertions.quote: several moments when energy prices dropped significantly and that closed that spark gap and made the air source heat pump cheaper to run

verdicts.note: Where time-of-use rates exist there may be an opportunity to shift heat pump use off-peak and improve bill savings; not analysed.

In RMI's models a tariff alone does not cut costs: a standard heat pump on Houston's Free Nights rate costs more than on a flat rate, and only flexible control on steep tariffs (3:1 TOU, Free Nights) saved about $1,000-2,000 over 15 years, while mild default TOU gave too little.

Mass Save: eligible customers can get a Seasonal Heat Pump Rate with lower electric rates November through April 'to help make heat pump operation more affordable'; time-of-use rates are only described as future options.

Staggered-adoption study of 6,631 UK households: switching to Octopus's Cosy heat pump time-of-use tariff saved about £318/yr (about 18% of the electricity bill), £78 from the tariff structure alone and £240 from shifting load; savings are vs the same supplier's flat tariff, and the authors are linked to Octopus.

assertions.quote: completely turns the tables in favor of an air source heat pump and it's combining one of those with solar

verdicts.note: In RMI's single Oakland retrofit scenario, a 6.5 kW solar array cut annual energy costs from $2,900 to $170 and brought net present cost below gas, but added over $15,000 upfront.

LBNL: the Electrification with PV cluster had the largest energy and cost savings, and solar is a reliable way to reduce energy cost, but its value depends on net-metering rules, and these whole projects still needed about $20k of cost cuts to break even.
UK households with solar PV had a smaller rise in daytime grid electricity after a heat pump, but no noticeable difference in overall consumption, though the authors note low power to detect it.
